cues: Design turns the requirements into a blueprint.
Logical design says what the system does, with diagrams that ignore the machine.
Physical design says how: tables, files, screens and modules.
Two words judge a design: high cohesion, each module doing one job, and low coupling, modules depending on each other as little as possible.
